chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Harun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
One who delays the Asr prayer so much that it misses him, Allah will bring him [without his family] and wealth on the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.تَفُوتَهُ: it misses him / he misses it
key_terms.غَیْرَ نَاسٍ: so much that / to the extent of

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of delaying the Asr prayer until it is missed?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the severe spiritual consequence of intentionally delaying the Asr prayer until its time expires. The phrase 'without his family and wealth' signifies that these primary worldly attachments will be rendered null and void for the neglecter on the Day of Judgment, serving as a potent reminder of the transient nature of dunya compared to the eternal reward of timely worship.
